Affordable Housing Conversion Program

​​​​

​​​​Program Overview

​The Wisconsin Community Development Block Grant (CDBG) Affordable Housing Conversion (AHC) program, mananged by the Department of Administraton's Division of Energy, Housing, and Community Resrouces (DEHCR) supports local governments in funding housing initatives primariliy benefiting low to moderate income (LMI) individuals. Grants are used for conversion housing that focuses on underutilized or vacant buildings to be converted into affordable housing development.

All activites funded with CDBG AHC funds must meet the National Objective of Low and Moderate Income Housing (LMH).  To qualify under the LMH national objective, at least 51% of the units to be rented must be occupied by households with incomes at or below 80% of the County Median Income (CMI) determined by household size.​


​Eligble​​​​ Activities 

  • Real Property Acquistion

  • Site Improvements and Development Hard Cost

  • Project related Soft Costs

  • Demolition costs when associated with reconstruction

  • Program Administration up to 3% of the CDBG awarded amount ​


Applicati​​​on Process

CDBG AHC funds are awar​ded through an annual competitive process.  Application materials and submission instructions should be carefully reviewed prior to applying for funds.

For each grant application received on or before the application submission deadline, DEHCR reviews, scores and ranks the applications based on a pre-approved list of scoring criteria. Successful applications must meet the above mentioned National Objective.  Applications earning the highest points in the review process are eligible for CDBG-AHC funding.​
